pairs.evidence: The Canvas WebView enables JavaScript and navigates to agent/gateway-supplied URLs. It exposed CanvasA2UIActionBridge ('openclawCanvasA2UIAction') whose postMessage forwarded any payload to handleCanvasA2UIActionFromWebView, whatever the page origin. Any loaded page could therefore inject agent actions (CVE-2026-35643). Fix 8b02ef13 (#52722, shipped v2026.3.22) gates the bridge on a trusted-origin check. The interface registration is unchanged, so this pair tests whether the scanner recognizes an in-bridge origin guard.

vulnerable_locations.function: query(SQLiteDatabase, Uri, String[], String, String[], String)

fixed_locations.note: The URI path segment is now bound as a parameter (_ID + "=?" with prependUriFirstSegmentToSelectionArgs). The caller-supplied 'where' is still concatenated, but delete() first validates it with VerificationUtils.verifyWhere for public URIs (line 137).

appendWhere(column + "=" + uri.getPathSegments().get(1)) is replaced by appendWhere(idColumn + "=?") plus a bound argument (lines 560-564). selection and sortOrder are token-validated (verifyWhere/verifySortOrder) for public URIs.

pairs.evidence: FileContentProvider is exported (AndroidManifest line 224-228). At the vulnerable commit it concatenated caller-controlled content-URI path segments into SQL, in db.delete(... _ID + "=" + uri.getPathSegments().get(1) + " AND (" + where + ")") and in SQLiteQueryBuilder.appendWhere(... + uri.getPathSegments().get(1)). It also passed caller-controlled selection/sortOrder through unvalidated, so other apps could inject SQL (GHSL-2021-1007, CVE-2021-43863). Fix merge 627caba6 ('Merge pull request from GHSA-vjp2-f63v-w479', stable-3.18, 3.18.1) parameterizes the URI segments and adds an SQLite tokenizer-based whitelist for where, sort and column names. Note: the sinks are SQLiteDatabase.delete and SQLiteQueryBuilder.appendWhere, not rawQuery/execSQL.

pairs.evidence: In process(event: Event), the outdated-request debug log used the Kotlin template '$event.ageLocalTs'. This interpolates event.toString() (a data class that includes the message 'content') followed by the literal '.ageLocalTs', so message content was written to the Timber/rageshake logs. PR #6706 'Fix cleartext leak in log' (changelog: 'Fix message content sometimes appearing in the log') changes it to '${event.ageLocalTs}'. No CVE. The sensitive value is the whole Event object, not a token/password-named variable.

rejected_candidates.reason: CVE-2019-15566 (HistorySearchProvider SQLi, PR #547). The fix only adds setStrict(true) and a projection map. The URI path-segment concatenation in query() (appendWhere COLUMN_ID + "=" + uri.getLastPathSegment()) and in update() is unchanged, so the fix is partial.
CVE-2023-23948/CVE-2023-24804 (GHSL-2022-059 FileContentProvider SQLi). GHSL reports the SQLi as not fixed in 3.0, and no fix commit could be identified.
CVE-2023-33188 (GHSL-2022-065). Out-of-scope class, and neither the advisory nor GHSL names a fix commit.

d4c2cb3c removes android:debuggable="true" from the main manifest, but the attribute was added and removed the same day (2026-05-16) and never shipped in a release. The removal was driven by lintVitalRelease rather than a security report, so it is too weak as a real-world ANDROID-DEBUG fix.

d514d5e1 cleanly removes NSAllowsArbitraryLoads (VideoCalls/Info.plist lines 53-57; parent 3fabce2b). The exception only existed in the very first development tag (v0.1, 2017-10-17), three days before removal and before v1.0.0, and there is no security rationale beyond the commit title. It would also duplicate the IOS-ATS family. Usable as a backup IOS-ATS pair.

GHSA-p9pv-h29j-jvqm (auth-step values logged) is fixed in 9f5c2739/a1586104 by adding CustomStringConvertible descriptions. The log call sites are unchanged, so no code location can be labeled cleanly. GHSA-pj5p-96xx-hc7m (canOpenURL system logging) is similarly indirect.
Rageshake backup-key exposure advisories (GHSA-42h8-mgpm-8gwv, GHSA-j9f4-49p7-x4cq): the bug and fix are in the matrix-rust-sdk dependency, not app code.

The 2-pairs-per-repo cap was reached. Other candidates were left out: GHSA-5j57-84cx-r295/CVE-2026-95815 (iOS deep-link URL with bearer key logged), GHSA-4p4f-fc8q-84m3 (iOS A2UI trust; fix is URL equality and trust plumbing, not a clean substring host-match change) and GHSA-83f3-hh45-vfw9 (Android ws:// accepted in code, not a manifest cleartext flag).

Second GHSL-2023-142 issue (WebViewActivity 'path' extra -> UrlUtil.handle accepting absolute URLs, changed in b6687dc7). It is interprocedural, and the fix is bundled with feature changes ('Shortcut path input improvements'), so it was not added as a separate pair.
CVE-2024-0245 (task hijacking via taskAffinity). It is out-of-scope, and the fix only changes the application-level taskAffinity (activity-level affinities remain), so it was not used.
GHSA-r8ff-qr7g-pvw6 (AMP XSS) not used: the input is email HTML, not platform-controlled input, and the bug is an HTML sanitizer flaw. The same repo is used for the out-of-scope path traversal pair.
GHSA-cx82-g79r-6v6w (OAuth token sent to the shared page host): no public fix commit identified, and the class is out of scope.
'Remove android:debuggable from manifest' (2014) is only available through third-party forks (the aosp-mirror org is gone), and it is a platform component rather than a standalone app.

No well-documented app-level vulnerable/fixed pair was found for AST-CRYPTO-ECB, AST-CRYPTO-WEAK-HASH/OBJC-CRYPTO-WEAK-HASH, IOS-KEYCHAIN-ACCESS, AST-WEBVIEW-HOST-ALLOWLIST/WEBVIEW-HOST-MATCH (the best real example, Wikipedia Android endsWith, is in an excluded repo), ANDROID-DEBUG or OBJC-WEBVIEW-UNTRUSTED-REQUEST. Commit-message and advisory searches returned only libraries, SDKs or deprecation-warning cleanups.
